en: The *Cundīdhāraṇīsūtra Spoken by the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*.
By [the monk] who held the rank of Kaifu Yitongsim, the special advancement (Tejin), the acting Minister of State Ceremonial (Shi Hongluqing),
Duke of Sushan with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, and posthumously honored as Minister of Works (Sikong).

Posthumously titled Great State Preceptor (Dàjiānzhèng), bearing the honorific title Great One of Vast Wisdom (Dàguǎngzhì) of the Great Xingshàn Monastery, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra translated [this] by imperial decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat...
In the city named Mahānāman, at the Jeta Grove in the Anāthapiṇḍada Park,
he was surrounded by a great assembly of bhikṣus, as well as bodhisattvas,
and the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others, preceding and following him.
Out of compassion for sentient beings of the future who possess meager merit and commit evil deeds,
he immediately entered the Cundī-samādhi and spoke the dhāraṇī taught by seven hundred million buddhas of the past, saying:
*Namo satvānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhakoṭīnām | tadyathā | oṃ cale cule cuḷe svāhā* | If there are bodhisattvas, whether monastics or laypeople, who practice the path of mantra, [they should recite this].
If one recites and maintains this dhāraṇī for ninety thousand full repetitions,
even the ten evil deeds, the four grave offenses, and the five crimes of immediate retribution committed over immeasurable kalpas will be extinguished.
All shall be completely extinguished.
In whatever place they are born, they will always encounter Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
possessing abundant wealth and treasures, they will always be able to leave the household life.
If a lay bodhisattva practices the precepts with firm resolve and without regression,
by reciting this dhāraṇī, they will always be reborn in the celestial realms.
Alternatively, one may constantly become a king among human beings;
one shall not fall into the evil realms, will draw near to the worthy and holy ones,
and will be cherished, honored, protected, and sustained by the devas.
If they engage in worldly affairs, they will be free from calamities and misfortunes;
their appearance will be upright and dignified, their speech majestic and solemn,
and their minds free from anxiety and distress.
If an ordained bodhisattva is fully endowed with the various prohibitive precepts,
reciting mantras at the three times of day and practicing according to the teachings,
the mundane and supramundane siddhis sought in the present life will surely manifest, and wisdom and insight will appear before them.
One will realize the stages and the perfections,
swiftly perfecting them and realizing unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If one recites this ten thousand times, [the same result shall be attained].
Immediately within the dream, one sees Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and vomits black substances;
this occurs if that person’s transgressions are particularly grave.
If one recites it twenty thousand times,
one will immediately see various celestial palaces and monasteries in a dream,
or climb a high mountain, or see oneself ascending a tree.
Sometimes they bathe in great ponds;
sometimes they see them soaring through the air;
or sometimes they see them sporting with celestial maidens.
Some see him preaching the Dharma; some see him plucking out his hair or shaving it off;
some see him eating curd-rice and drinking white nectar;
or some see him crossing over great oceans and rivers.
Sometimes they ascend a lion throne, or see the Bodhi tree;
sometimes they ride in a boat, or see a śramaṇa;
or they see a householder with his head covered by white or yellow robes.
Sometimes they see the sun and moon, or boys and girls;
sometimes there are milk and fruit trees above them;
or they see a black man vomiting flames from his mouth.
One may fight with them and emerge victorious;
or one may see a vicious horse or a water buffalo coming to gore and strike.
The practitioner may see [the deity] strike or scold them and flee in terror;
or consume milk gruel and curd-rice;
or see *sumana* flowers.
If one sees a king,
or if such visions do not appear,
it should be known that this person committed the five crimes of immediate retribution in a previous life.
One should further recite it until seventy thousand times are completed;
one will then see the aforementioned visions and should know that the transgressions have been extinguished.
This constitutes the preliminary practice.
Thereafter, one should paint the primary image according to the ritual rules,
whether at three sessions, four sessions, or six sessions.
By making offerings according to the Dharma, one shall obtain all mundane and supramundane siddhis,
up to and including unsurpassed bodhi.
If there are those who practice and maintain this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain these fruits].
One should know that regarding the future accomplishment of the site,
whether there are obstacles or not, and whether the *siddhi* will be slow or swift,
one should [perform this] in a single pure room.
Smeared a small altar with cow dung and made offerings according to one's means; then,
using the *dhāraṇī* for binding the boundary, one bound the realms of the ten directions.
Place a single bottle of scented water within the maṇḍala and recite [the mantra] with a single-minded focus.
If the bottle moves or turns, one should know that the purpose for which it was performed and the sought-after matter have been accomplished.
If one does not remain motionless, the rite will not be accomplished.
Furthermore, as for the ritual method:
take a single earthen bowl, smear it with incense, and place it within the maṇḍala.
Recite with single-minded concentration.
If the bowl rotates, the rite is accomplished;
if it does not move, the rite is not accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to know future events,
one should first smear a small altar and have a youth of auspicious marks and merit bathe thoroughly,
cleanse himself, and don fresh, clean garments.
With seven *koṭi* of mantras,
empower the incense smeared upon the boy's hands;
furthermore, empower the flowers seven times.
Place it in the hands of the youth and have him stand within the mandala with his face covered. Then,
take another flower and recite the mantra.
Perform the empowerment once for each strike on the back of the youth’s hand,
up to twenty-one times; then,
inquire of the youth regarding matters of good or evil fortune.
The youths all spoke thus.
Furthermore, there is a method: take a bright mirror and place it within the maṇḍala.
First, recite the mantra over flowers one hundred and eight times to empower them.
Thereafter, he again recited the mantra; with each recitation,
he struck the surface of the mirror once,
and immediately characters appeared upon the mirror's surface.
One speaks of matters of good and evil.
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, if one wishes to know whether a matter is auspicious or inauspicious, successful or unsuccessful,
one should take *sumana* flower-scented oil.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times to empower it,
then apply it to the surface of the right thumb while reciting the mantra with an uninterrupted voice.
He caused the youth to look at his finger,
upon which appeared the forms of various Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
or he manifested written characters that fully explained good and evil.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person suffers from a disease caused by malevolent spirits,
one should take willow branches or blades of reed grass and,
while reciting the mantra, brush them over the patient's body.
One will immediately achieve recovery.
Furthermore, if one suffers from a grave illness,
one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
If one performs a *homa* with cow’s milk while reciting the person's name, they will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, if a child cries at night,
have a young girl twist a thread from right to left.
Recite the mantra to empower it,
tie twenty-one knots, and fasten them beneath the child's neck;
the child will then no longer cry at night.
Furthermore, there is another method: first, empower white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times.
Then, taking the mustard seeds, recite the mantra once for each seed as you cast them to strike that malevolent spirit.
If one recites it twenty-one times, the malevolent spirits will flee and the patient will recover.
Furthermore, there is another method for those afflicted by ghosts.
Smeared a small altar with *gomaya* (cow dung),
drew the form of a malevolent spirit on the ground using flour and charcoal,
and recited the mantra while striking it with pomegranate wood and other materials.
That ghost wept and fled away. Furthermore,
if a person is possessed by a malevolent spirit, or if one is afflicted by illness,
[one should perform this rite].
Being at a distance, one cannot come there oneself;
nor does the practitioner go to that place.
Instead, one takes a branch of willow, a branch of peach, or a flower.
Empower it one hundred and eight times.
Have someone take it to the patient's location and brush the patient with the branch.
Alternatively, one may have the patient smell the flower,
or strike the patient with the flower;
the possessing spirit will then depart, and the patient will recover.
Furthermore, there is another method:
if one has been bitten by a snake or seized by a *nāgī* demoness,
one should circumambulate the patient while reciting the mantra.
The illness will then be healed.

Furthermore, there is another method: if a person suffers from boils, swellings, and the like, or is bitten by various venomous insects, one should take sandalwood sap and mix it with earth to form a paste.
Recite the mantra seven times and apply it to the sore; it will heal immediately.
Furthermore, if one is traveling on a road, one should recite this mantra.
One will not be robbed or harmed by thieves,
nor will one encounter difficulties from various predatory birds and beasts.
Furthermore, if one engages in conflict, litigation, or legal disputes, this dharma shall resolve the matter through principle.
Furthermore, when engaging in debate to seek victory, one will prevail mightily by reciting this mantra.
Moreover, there is another method: if one travels upon a river, [one should recite it].
By reciting this mantra, one will not be swept away by floods, nor harmed by evil nāgas, makaras, tortoises, or crocodiles within the water.
Furthermore, as for the method [to be used] if one is imprisoned or confined:
By reciting this dhāraṇī, one will swiftly attain liberation.
Furthermore, if there is an epidemic in a country,
one should for seven nights [offer] sesame and non-glutinous rice.
Perform *homa* with ghee and honey;
thus calamities will be extinguished and the land will be at peace.
Furthermore, regarding the method for those who seek abundant wealth and treasures:
If one performs homa with various kinds of food every day,
one will obtain an abundance of wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, there is a method for causing others to feel respect, love, and joy.
If one recites the person's name within the mantra,
they will immediately become joyful and submit.
Furthermore, as for the method regarding those who have no clothing:
By reciting the mantra, one immediately obtains clothing.
Furthermore, whatever one seeks in one's mind,
all will be obtained as desired through recitation.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person suffers pain in the limbs or joints,
one should empower the hands twenty-one times;
by rubbing and touching the painful area, the ailment will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, if one suffers from malaria or headaches,
one may touch the afflicted area with a hand empowered twenty-one times;
thus, one will also be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method:
smear a small altar and take a copper bowl, filling it to the brim with pure ash.
Have the youth press both hands down upon the bowl of ash.
The reciter should chant the mantra;
the deity’s messenger enters the body of the youth,
whereupon the bowl immediately turns and descends, speaking to the youth.
At daybreak, he himself binds the samaya-mudrās of the three families and recites the mantras of the three families;
he then takes a smooth stone and hands it over to the youth.
The youth then inscribed upon the ground past and future events— whether auspicious or inauspicious, good or evil—
as well as lost or forgotten sūtras and śāstras, difficult points, mantras, and mudrās.
One will immediately attain understanding and realization.
Furthermore, there is a method: when two armies are opposed to one another, write this dhāraṇī on birch bark, suspend it from a bamboo pole, and have a person hold it in their hand.
By reciting the mantra, that enemy will be immediately destroyed.
Furthermore, there is another method: if a woman has no son or daughter, one should use ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*) upon birch bark.
Write this mantra and wear it;
before long, you shall have a son or daughter.
Furthermore, there is another method: if there is a woman whose husband does not hold her in high regard...
Take a new flask and fill it completely with water.
Place within the flask the seven precious gems, various efficacious herbs, the five grains, and white mustard seeds.
Tie the neck of the flask with silk cloth.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with the mantra.
Have the woman form the root mudrā and place it upon her crown,
then perform the water consecration.
She immediately gained favor, love, and respect;
not only was she held in high esteem, but she also conceived a child whose development in the womb was firm and stable.
Furthermore, whenever a practitioner of the Dharma recites mantras,
they should bind the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and recite the mantra;
having performed this for the stūpa-seal sixty thousand times, it shall be complete.
Whatever one seeks shall be fully accomplished.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, and Tārā Bodhisattva will manifest their forms before one,
so that all requests are fulfilled according to one's wishes.
Some become kings within the palaces of the asuras;
some attain the stages of a bodhisattva;
and some obtain medicines for longevity.
Alternatively, one may achieve the accomplishment of the rite for gaining respect and affection.
Furthermore, there is a method [to perform this] at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) or before a great stūpa.
By reciting this dhāraṇī,
one shall behold the noble Saṅgha and converse with them, attain the accomplishment of siddhi,
and be able to practice together with them.
One will then become one with that noble Saṃgha.
Furthermore, if one performs recitation atop a high mountain peak for one koṭi of times,
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva will lead this person along with five hundred and sixty others.
Together they shall dwell in the palace of the asuras for a lifespan of one kalpa,
where they will behold Maitreya Bodhisattva.
One hears the True Dharma;
having heard the Dharma, one attains the Bodhisattva stages and achieves non-retrogression.
Furthermore, regarding Mount Vipula, it is said that even at any high mountain, one may perform recitations before a stūpa or image containing śarīra.
One should offer incense and flowers according to one's means and sustain the body and life by begging for alms,
from the first day of the month until the fifteenth.
Recite the dhāraṇī until it reaches three hundred thousand times.
On the day the count is complete, fast for one full day and night and increase your offerings twofold.
In the latter part of the night,
one will see the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi lead the practitioner to his own palace and show the practitioner the entrance to the Asura cave.
Entering the cave, one attains the wondrous nectar of the gods and a lifespan equal to that of the sun and moon.
Furthermore, there is a method regarding the jeweled stupa at the place where [the Buddha] descended from heaven via the triple-jeweled staircase:
the practitioner should beg for alms, circumambulate it, and recite [the mantra] ten million times.
He immediately beheld the Bodhisattva Invincible,
who, in accordance with his wish, expounded the sublime Dharma and revealed the path to unsurpassed bodhi.
Or they may see Hārītī leading this person into her own palace and giving them a longevity elixir,
whereby they return to childhood, youthful, handsome, and pleasing.
Having obtained the permission of the Great Being who guards the hidden treasure (pātala),
one should extensively benefit the Triple Gem.
One shall receive the consolation of all Bodhisattvas, who will show the way of the true path.
Even unto the seat of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, if a person lacks past roots of goodness,
lacks the seed of enlightenment, and does not cultivate the practices for enlightenment;
Reciting it even once gives rise to the sprout of the Dharma of Bodhi;
how much more so for those who can constantly recite, maintain, and uphold it.
Regarding the Ritual Manual for Reciting the Seven-Crore Cundī Dhāraṇī: if there are those who practice this dhāraṇī seeking its accomplishment, [they should proceed as follows].
First, one must bathe and don clean robes.
Adorn the ritual site (*maṇḍala*) and install the principal deity according to what one's means allow.
This is the method for the ritual site.
One should select an auspicious site and construct a mandala measuring four cubits on each side.
Dig three cubits deep and remove all broken tiles, rubble, poor soil, hair, body down, bone ash, charcoal, insects, ants, and the like.
Fill the pit with high-quality, pure earth and level it firmly.
If one digs up soil that is not foul and uses it to fill [the site] with old earth,
and if the soil is superior, one should know that the ground is greatly auspicious and will swiftly bring accomplishment.
Take cow dung that has not yet fallen to the ground,
mix it with scented water, sand, and fine earth to form a paste,
and recite the mantra of the Bodhisattva Aparājita.
Consecrate it twenty-one times.
Then, smear the altar.

Having smeared it, take the five purifiers and mix them together. As for the five purifiers: cow dung, cow urine, curd, milk, and ghee. Consecrate these one hundred and eight times with the mantra of the Bodhisattva Aparājita.
Smear it all around the maṇḍala in a clockwise direction.
Whether it is established upon a mountain rock,
or in a multi-storied pavilion, or situated upon a boat.
This is the place where all worthy and holy ones attain the Way.
Simply smear it with the five pure substances and sit facing east.
Form the Invincible Seal (*aparājita-mudrā*) and press it upon the ground;
recite the mantra seven times to consecrate the center of the mandala.
Furthermore, take small portions of various medicinal herbs, the seven precious gems, and the five grains.
Dig a hole at the center one cubit deep and place therein various medicinal herbs and the seven precious gems.
Then take the original soil to fill it back up and level it out.
Pressing with the right hand, recite the verse for the Earth Deity three times.
The verse for awakening the Earth Deity says:
"O Deity, you who are our close protector, [you who dwell] among the teachers of the Buddhas' path..."
Practicing the supreme conduct, purifying the stages and perfections as one shatters the hosts of Māra, I— the Lion of the Śākyas,
the Savior of the World— likewise subdue Māra; I draw the maṇḍala.
Recite the mantra of Kṣitigarbha:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ pṛthivītejo-vijaye svāhā*. Having recited this verse, perform the empowerment.
Thereafter, smear sandalwood paste upon the nine sacred positions,
which are like the full moon. Using new and pure offering vessels—
whether of gold, silver, refined copper, brass, shell, jade, stone, porcelain, wood, or other such new implements.
One should arrange offerings according to one's means, providing various foods and drinks, as well as fragrant herbs, lamps, candles, argha water, and scented water.
This applies to both lay and ordained bodhisattvas who seek spiritual accomplishment.
Whenever entering a dharma hall, one should first pay homage to the Buddha.
Having performed repentance, rejoicing in merit, requesting the turning of the wheel, and making vows, one should take the vow to receive the Bodhicitta precepts. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ muditā-mudrā-namasyami. One whose bodhicitta is thus [generated] is free from all grasping at a self and is detached from the aggregates, sense bases, and elements.
Furthermore, being free from the grasper and the grasped,
they are equal regarding all phenomena,
because their own minds are fundamentally unarisen and empty of intrinsic nature.
"Just as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past gave rise to the bodhicitta,
so do I. This is called the self-vow for receiving the bodhicitta precepts.
By reciting this once while contemplating the ultimate truth,
one attains immeasurable, boundless, unconditioned merit,
which adorns the three karmas.
Until reaching the seat of enlightenment, their merit shall be uninterrupted;
all karmic obstructions will be swiftly extinguished,
and they will quickly attain accomplishment in the mantras.
The tutelary deity appears before one,
just as in the "Entry into the Dharma Realm" chapter [of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra],
where the Bodhisattva Maitreya [appeared] to the youth Sudhana.
Having spoken of the merits of the bodhicitta and having taken the vows of the bodhicitta precepts,
sit in either the full-lotus or half-lotus posture as you prefer.
Straightening the body and closing the eyes, one should immediately form the mudrā of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*).
One should visualize the Mother Buddha Cundī in the sky, surrounded by seven koṭis of Buddhas,
filling the entirety of space.
Within meditative concentration, one should pay homage to all Buddhas and the Buddha-mother Cundī.
Thereafter, having smeared the hands [with sandalwood paste],
one should form the ritual mudrās.
The Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family: Join the two hands with palms hollowed;
extend the two index fingers and bend them so that they rest against the side of the first phalanges of the middle fingers.
Place both thumbs against the base of the two index fingers, and this is accomplished.
Recite the mantra seven times at the heart while visualizing the Tathāgata’s thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs of excellence.
The marks and signs [of the Buddha] appear as distinct as if facing one's very eyes.
The mantra is:
Oṃ tathāgatodbhava svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the result is attained].
Thereupon, they awaken all Tathāgatas,
who shall all protect, mindfully attend to, and empower the practitioner,
touching them with their radiance.
All karmic obstacles and hindrances shall be completely extinguished;
one’s lifespan shall be long and far-reaching, and merit and wisdom shall increase.
The holy assemblies of the Buddha Family shall protect one with joy.
May one be separated from all evil destinies in birth after birth;
may one be born by transformation within a lotus and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
As for the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family: join the two hands with palms hollowed and joined.
Spread apart the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers,
bending them into the shape of a lotus.
Placing the mudrā at the heart, recite the mantra seven times.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara as being fully endowed with the primary and secondary marks of perfection.
To scatter [offerings] at the right side of his crown, recite the mantra:
Oṃ bhadanamo nābhavāya svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
Immediately, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Holder of the Lotus, was awakened;
touched by the radiance of all bodhisattvas,
all his karmic obstructions were completely extinguished.
All bodhisattvas are always one's virtuous friends.
For the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family,
turn the left hand outward and place the back of the right palm against the back of the left hand.
Interlace the left and right thumbs and little fingers so that they form the shape of a vajra, placing it at the heart.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and recite the mantra seven times.
The mantra for the mudrā of scattering at the crown of the head is:
Oṃ vairocanābhava svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the following occurs].
This immediately awakens all the noble Vajra assemblies,
who empower and protect one so that all karmic obstacles and transgressions are completely extinguished,
and no suffering shall ever touch the body.
One shall then attain a body as firm and solid as a vajra.
Next, bind the second root mudrā to protect the body:
interlace the two hands with the backs facing outward.
Joining the two index fingers and the two thumbs together and holding them straight upward forms the mudrā.
Recite the Heart Mantra of the Mother and seal the five places of the body with it.
That is to say: first the forehead, then the right shoulder, then the left shoulder, then the heart, then the throat.
The mantra for scattering upon the crown of the head is:
Oṃ kama-re vimale jvāle svāhā. When performing the seal for binding and protecting the body:
Arouse a heart of great compassion,
universally taking as its object the six realms and four modes of birth.
May all sentient beings don the firm adamantine armor of the great vow’s adornment.
One shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Next, bind the seal of the earth-bound kila:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Join the two thumbs, the two index fingers, and the two little fingers together. Then,
bend the left index finger into the shape of a hook.
Twice more, pull back the thumb;
this forms the Earth-Touching Mudrā.
Pull it back once while reciting the mantra one time. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ jñānīṃ jikrāya svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra to consecrate the boundary of the earth, it extends downward to the water’s edge like a vajra seat.
He will not be harmed or disturbed by celestial māras or other obstructors,
and with little exertion of effort, he will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, the practitioner of recitation should visualize a great eight-petaled lotus at the center of the maṇḍala.
Above was a lion throne,
upon which stood a jeweled pavilion,
from which hung various necklaces, silk banners, flags, and canopies.
Rows of precious pillars hung with exquisite celestial robes;
clouds of incense spread everywhere, raining down various flowers,
while all manner of music was played.
With precious vases, *argha* offerings, divine delicacies, and lamps made of *maṇi* jewels—
should there be no maṇḍala,
it is accomplished simply by visualizing them within the sky.
Having performed this visualization, one should recite this verse:
By the power of my merit, The power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
And the power of the Dharma-realm, I abide in universal offering.
Having recited this verse, one then recites the mantra of the Bodhisattva Mahāgaganagañja:
Oṃ gaganasvabhāva-vajra hūṃ. By the empowerment of reciting this mantra, [the following is accomplished].
The offerings one intends to present are truly no different from reality;
all the noble assembly shall partake of them.
Next, bind the mudrā of the precious chariot.
Cross the two hands with the palms facing upward.
Place the two index fingers horizontally against each other,
and with the two thumbs, each press down at the base of the respective index finger.
Visualize a carriage of the seven precious gems;
the messengers of the Buddha-family drive this carriage of the seven precious gems,
ascending into the void and departing.
Then, at the summit of the Form Realm, within the palace of Vairocana Buddha in the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, one recites the mantra seven times. The mantra is:
Oṃ tūru tūru hūṃ. By reciting this mantra and performing the mudrā-consecration, [the rite is accomplished].
The seven-jeweled chariot reaches the summit of the Form Realm (rūpadhātu).
The Buddha-Mother Cundī, together with the eight great bodhisattvas and the assembly of various holy beings as her retinue,
surrounds [her] and mounts the seven-jeweled chariot.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the chariot.
Following the previous mudrā, bend the thumb toward the body;
by extending the middle finger, it is formed.
Recite the mantra seven times. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ siddhyādhipataye tathāgatāya oṃ vairocanīya-karṣaya svāhā*. By virtue of empowering [the object] through the recitation of this mantra...
The assembly of noble ones comes from their native lands and dwells in mid-air above the site of enlightenment.
Next, one forms the mudrā for inviting the primary deity.
Descending from the carriage at the site of practice (maṇḍala), perform the first root mudrā as previously described;
beckon with the two thumbs toward the body and recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jvala-jvalani-ihayi he bhagavati svāhā. Next, one should bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Aparājita to expel obstructing spirits.
Interlace the two hands with the right pressing over the left, forming fists;
extend the two middle fingers so that their tips touch, and it is thus completed.
Rotate this around the body three times to the left while performing this visualization.
All obstructors, vināyakas, and malevolent spirits fled far away;
the assembly of noble ones who had arrived remained, abiding in their original samaya through great compassion.
I pray that you grant your protection.
*Namo samantabuddhānām, oṃ hulu hulu caṇḍāli maṇḍaki svāhā*. Next, perform the mudrā for binding the boundary walls.
Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā,
bend the right index finger and extend the left index finger;
rotate three times to the right.
According to the proximity or distance of one's mind, it immediately becomes a vajra-like fortress of adamantine solidity.
Even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress it,
let alone other beings who are difficult to subdue.
Vighnas, venomous insects, and those with sharp fangs and claws cannot approach; the mantra is:
Oṃ jvālini-prakara-svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the net for the upper direction.
Following the previous wall-boundary seal,
extend the left index finger;
press the right [finger] against the middle joint of the left, crossing them, and it is thus completed.
Recite this mantra three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ cundini jvala svāhā. By reciting the mantra and performing the mudrā with empowerment, [the rite is accomplished].
This immediately forms a vajra net, firm, solid, and indestructible.
Next, bind the mudrā of the secret seam of the fire enclosure:
place the left hand over the back of the right hand so that they overlap.
Simply by erecting the two thumbs, it is accomplished.
Recite the mantra three times and circumambulate to the right three times.
Visualize that outside the vajra wall, there is a surrounding blaze of vajra fire.
The mantra is:
Oṃ asamañji hūṃ phaṭ. Having bound this mudrā and recited the mantra, one achieves great binding and protection, [resulting in] a secret seam.
One shall not be entered by any demons.
Next, bind the *argha* mudrā:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Hold the tips of the two middle fingers together.
Use the two index fingers to press against the backs of the two middle fingers.
Place the sides of the two thumbs against the base of the two index fingers.
This constitutes the Root Mudrā.
Following the previous Root Mudrā,
slightly bend the two thumbs and insert them into the palms.
Then, form the arghya mudrā and recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ namo bhagavatyai ārya-prajñāpāramitāyai svāhā. The practitioner contemplates the assembly of noble ones with perfect clarity, visualizing themselves beneath the feet of the Buddhas and the noble assembly.
Holding a vessel of seven precious substances filled with scented water,
one bathes the feet of the noble assembly;
by virtue of offering this scented water in the *argha* vessel, [the merit is attained].
The practitioner purifies the three karmas and washes away the defilements of affliction;
the karmic obstructions are extinguished.
Next, one binds the Lotus Seat Mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā,
extend both index fingers upward toward the body.
Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable lion thrones flow forth.
I offer this to all the noble assembly.
Each member of this noble assembly sits down.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kāmala svāhā. By reciting this mantra while forming the seat-seal (āsana-mudrā) to make offerings to the assembly of noble ones,
the practitioner shall attain the fulfillment of the ten stages (daśabhūmi).
One attains the vajra-seat.
Following the previous root mudrā,
join the tips of the two thumbs.
Form the mudrā by pressing the middle joints of the two middle fingers together.
Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Reciting "Oṃ svāhā," one should visualize that from this mudrā,
immeasurable rays of light stream forth;
within each path of light, there are immeasurable auspicious vases made of the seven precious gems.
Visualize exquisite perfumed water filling the heavens,
pouring over all the noble assemblies to bathe them.
Furthermore, visualize that there are immeasurable celestial music in the sky,
making offerings to the Honored One, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones.
This is because of binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra.
Before long, the practitioner shall realize the Dharma-cloud stage (dharmameghā-bhūmi).
Next, bind the ointment mudrā (gandha-mudrā),
following the previous root mudrā.
Using the two thumbs, press them firmly against the lower joint of the right index finger; this constitutes the mantra, which is recited three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ hrīḥ svāhā. Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable rays of light stream forth;
upon each path of light, there are immeasurable clouds and oceans of sublime celestial unguents and powdered incense.
One makes offerings to the principal deity, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones.
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra,
one shall realize the fragrance of the morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation of all Tathāgatas.
Next, form the Flower Mudrā.
It is formed according to the previous Root Mudrā,
by placing the two thumbs flat against the lower joints of the left index fingers.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ jūḥ svāhā. Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Along each and every path of light, there are immeasurable oceans of exquisite celestial flower clouds,
making offerings to the primary deity, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones.
This occurs by virtue of binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra.
One shall attain the accomplishment of the Great Compassion Samādhi,
thereby able to bring benefit and happiness to boundless sentient beings,
and no calamities or misfortunes shall affect one's person.
Next, form the incense mudrā.
It is formed according to the root mudrā:
bend the right index finger to pinch the tips of the two thumbs. This completes it.
Recite the mantra three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ hrīḥ svāhā. Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Upon each path of light, there are immeasurable, harmoniously blended, co-emergent oceans of celestial clouds of exquisite incense,
making offerings to the Honored Ones, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of holy beings.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra,
one shall attain the accomplishment of the Samādhi of the Pervasive Dharmadhātu.
Next, bind the food and drink mudrā, following the previous root mudrā.
Form it by pressing the tips of the two thumbs with the left index finger.
Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ juna svāhā. Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Along each path of light, there are immeasurable clouds and oceans of various kinds of celestial, wondrous food and drink.
By making offerings to the principal deity, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones,
one shall obtain the food of the joy of Dharma and the bliss of dhyāna,
and the most supreme flavor of the three gates of liberation.
The samādhi is accomplished.
Next, bind the lamp mudrā according to the previous root mudrā.
Form it by pressing the tips of the two index fingers against the tips of the two thumbs.
Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:
Recite "Aṃ svāhā. Visualize that from this mudrā, immeasurable rays of light stream forth.
Within each path of light, there are immeasurable clouds and oceans of various kinds of lamps and candles made of the seven precious gems.
Make offerings to the principal deity, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of noble ones;
you shall then attain the radiance of the Prajñāpāramitā and the purification of the five eyes.
Next, recite the hymn of praise.
Avatara adhiṣṭhāna-samāraṃbha-kuñci-praṇāma-pada-vihite ājñapte sari suni jūli siddhe sāramanti.
Svāśamani svāhante saparanave tadyathā kṣāraṇa ṭe avindata stambhana maṇi rasana roga trāṇa svāhā.
Jālandhara-karṇikāra-vināśubhinī-pratara-karadoṣiṇī-sampuṭa-siddha-tva-prajñāti-māratam.
*Gaseṭṭhe likhāraṇi nandite nāpārapākūṃḍe śīle ya-sattvaṃti ramiyañ-jabhe ta.*
mūṃ nīlavajriṇaṃ suvarṇaprabhāvanapariveśayanty-ariyavaruṇitī-puṣṭi-nasaṃśayaṃ saptarājaḥ.

Recite: *tatsidhi kalpura ya manu rāgaṃ si na ti na ta vaṃ sama raṅka śi tvaṃ*.
Next, the method for arranging the syllables of the mantra of the tutelary deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) is explained.
From the crown of the head down to the feet, one contemplates each syllable of the mantra,
distinct in its curves and clearly manifesting radiant light that illuminates the sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth within the cycle of saṃsāra.
Arousing deep compassion, bestow peace and happiness by arranging the nine syllables of the dhāraṇī upon the body of the practitioner.
One then becomes a body empowered by the eight great bodhisattvas through the seal of the Tathāgata.
If one performs the rite for pacification (śāntika),...
Through the four types of rites— namely, those of pacifying, increasing, subjugating, and magnetizing— corresponding respectively to the colors white, yellow, black, and red,
one accomplishes *siddhi*.
Then, one forms the *Vyūhākṣara-mudrā*:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
join the two thumbs, the two index fingers, and the two little fingers together, and it is thus completed.
Visualize the syllable Oṃ at the crown of the head and touch the top of the head with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable AṂ above both eyes;
having visualized it, again touch the tops of the right and left eyes with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable *LĪ* placed at the throat and touch it with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable *JHU* at the heart and touch it with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable *LĪ* placed on the left and right shoulders and touch them with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable *źaṃ* placed upon the navel and touch it with the thumb.
Next, visualize the syllable *niḥ* placed upon both the right and left thighs and touch them with the little fingers.
Next, visualize the syllable *svā* placed upon the right and left thighs, touching them with the little fingers.
Next, visualize the syllable *ha* placed upon the soles of the right and left feet, touching them with the little fingers.
By means of visualizing the mantra and performing the mudrā-consecration,
the practitioner’s body immediately becomes the body of the Tathāgata Mother,
and all karmic obstructions are extinguished.
Having accumulated immeasurable merit and auspiciousness,
his body becomes an indestructible vajra essence.
If one can constantly focus the mind upon this contemplative practice, [the result will be attained].
All siddhis will appear before you,
and you shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Next, bind the root mudrā.
Recite the root mantra seven times and perform the scattering mudrā over the crown of the head.
Then, take a rosary of bodhi seeds consisting of one hundred and eight beads and string them together according to the ritual rules.
Immediately, smear the fragrant unguent upon the beads.
Holding the beads in the palms of both hands at the level of the heart, recite the mantra seven times to consecrate the rosary. The mantra for consecrating the rosary is as follows:
Oṃ vairocana-maḥ svāhā. Having empowered [the object] with this, one places it upon the crown of the head and makes this vow with body and speech:
"I now wish to perform the recitation."
I pray that the Honored Ones, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, will grant their empowerment and mindful protection.
May I swiftly attain the fulfillment of all siddhis as desired.
Then, support the beads with the ring finger and thumb of the left hand.
With the right hand, move the beads using the thumb and ring finger;
the hand should be in the *dharmacakra-pravartana* (turning the wheel of Dharma) mudrā.
One should hold the rosary before the heart while reciting.
The sound is neither slow nor hurried;
the mind is focused one-pointedly without distraction.
One contemplates one's own body as being identical to the body of the deity, complete with all its physical marks and signs of excellence.
Furthermore, within the front mandala before one's body,
visualize the Mother of Seven Koṭis surrounded by her retinue,
sitting clearly and distinctly face-to-face.
Each time one utters the syllable *svāhā*, one should simultaneously move one bead [along the rosary].
One should always fix the number of recitations at either one hundred and eight or one thousand and eight.
If it does not reach one hundred and eight,
it will not suffice for the required number of recitations for attaining *siddhi*.
Having finished the recitation, coil the rosary within the palms.
Bearing this upon my head, I make this vow, saying:
"By the merit of my recitation,
may all sentient beings accomplish the mantras they cultivate."
By practicing this, one will swiftly attain accomplishment in the superior,
middling, or inferior siddhis. Place the jewel within a casket,
then form the mudrā of concentration, straighten the body, close the eyes, and clarify the mind with a settled intention.
Within the chest of the body, there appears a brilliant, perfect clarity, as pure and radiant as the full moon;
one should arouse great diligence to decisively attain realization.
If one can apply oneself with focused effort without indolence, [success will follow].
One will certainly perceive the fundamentally pure mind of the source.
Within this perfect luminosity, one should visualize the syllable Oṃ,
with the remaining eight syllables arranged in a clockwise rotation.
Arrange them in rows upon the perfectly luminous [sphere].
Within meditative concentration, one must clearly perceive the syllables of the mantra.
Once the concentration is attained and there is no longer distraction, [the visualization is complete].
This is then in accord with the Prajñāpāramitā.
One should immediately draw a full, bright lunar disc.
Next, one should contemplate the meaning of the seed-syllables of the alphabet.
The syllable Oṃ signifies the meaning of the three bodies (trikāya) and also the meaning that all phenomena are fundamentally unborn.
The syllable Kha signifies the meaning that all phenomena are neither born nor extinguished.
The syllable *Li* (𑖮) signifies the meaning that the characteristics of all phenomena (*dharma*) are unattainable.
The syllable *Zhu* (𑖯) signifies the meaning that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing.
The syllable *Li* (𑖮) signifies the meaning that all phenomena are without defilement.
The syllable *cuṃ* signifies that all phenomena are equal and awakened.
The syllable *niḥ* signifies that all phenomena are without grasping or abandoning.
The syllable *svā* signifies that all phenomena are equal and beyond verbal expression.
The syllable *Ha* signifies that all phenomena (*dharma*) are without cause.
Because all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen, they are neither born nor extinguished.
Because they are neither born nor extinguished, their characteristics are found to be non-apprehendible.
Because signs are non-apprehendable, one attains the absence of arising and ceasing.
Because there is no arising or ceasing, one attains stainlessness.
Because there is stainlessness, one attains peerless awakening.
Because there is no equal awakening, one attains non-acceptance and non-rejection.
Because there is no acceptance or rejection, one attains equanimity beyond verbal expression.

Because there is equanimity beyond verbal expression, one attains the non-apprehension that accords with *prajñā*, being without cause or effect; through this skillful means, one enters the ultimate reality and realizes the *dharmadhātu-tathatā*. Having completed the recitation for this *samādhi*, one should bind the root mudrā.
Next, form the mudrā for bathing.
Next, form the mudrās for the five offerings.
Next, recite praises and offer arghya water.
Next, bind the *asamoghini* mudrā and turn it counter-clockwise once to dissolve the boundary.
Next, bind the precious chariot (*ratnasyandana*) mudrā by pointing the thumb outward and flicking the tips of the middle fingers.
To escort the Noble One back to his original palace, the mantra for the escorting is as follows:
Oṃ cale cule culu svāhā. Then, bind the *samaya* mudrās of the three families.
Each person shall recite the mantra once while circumambulating.
They should prostrate to the Buddha as before, perform repentance, rejoice in merit, request [the Buddhas] to remain, make vows, and dedicate the merit toward unsurpassed bodhi.
Then, they may walk at will or recite Mahāyāna sūtras such as the *Avataṃsaka* and the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
Bathe the śarīra within the seal, stūpa, or image;
circumambulate clockwise while contemplating the six recollections.
Dedicate this accumulation of merit toward the attainment of one's desired siddhi.
Next, the four methods of pacifying (śāntika), increasing (pauṣṭika), magnetizing (vaśya), and subjugating (abhicāra) are explained.
Regarding the śāntika rite:
it is for seeking the extinction of sins, the transformation of obstacles, and the removal of calamities.
Possession by malevolent spirits and illness;
imprisonment, shackles, pestilence, and national calamities;
irregularity of floods and droughts; and damage to the crops by insects.
When the five planets oppress one's natal destiny,
all afflictions are entirely extinguished and one attains liberation;
this is called the rite for pacifying calamities (śāntika).
When performing this rite,
one should wear white garments, face north,
and sit in the auspicious posture (bhadrapīṭha) with legs crossed and knees raised.
Visualize the deity as white.
All offerings— food, drink, cakes, incense, flowers, lamps, candles, the ground,
and so forth— are entirely white.
From the first day of the month until the eighth, recite three times each day and perform *homa* at night using the *śāntika* mantra, which says:
*Oṃ cale cule cuḷe amukaṃ śāntiṃ kuru svāhā*. For the *pauṣṭika* rite, [the mantra is]: *Oṃ cale cule cuḷe amukaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ kuru svāhā*. If reciting for another person, call that person’s name.
One seeks longevity, official rank and glory, hidden treasures, abundance, and intelligence;
the accomplishment of the dhāraṇī of hearing and retaining without forgetting;
and the accomplishment of the vajra and other [implements].
Or they may manifest as lions, elephants, horses, or other such forms;
through the empowerment of mantras, these three signs appear,
and according to whether the aspiration is superior, middling, or inferior, the corresponding fruit is obtained.
As explained extensively in the *Siddhi*,
those who wish to enter the caves of the *vidyādhara* sages,
as well as the caves of the eight classes of spirits and deities (*aṣṭabhūta*), shall all succeed in doing so.
Furthermore, having realized the stages and attained supernormal powers,
one seeks the perfection of the two kinds of provisions to swiftly achieve unsurpassed enlightenment.
This is called the rite of augmentation.
When performing this rite,
one should wear yellow robes, face east, and sit in the full lotus posture.
Visualize the deity as yellow;
the incense, flowers, food, fruits, lamps, candles, ground,
and all other offerings presented are likewise entirely yellow.
From the eighth day to the fifteenth day of the month, recite the mantra three times each day and perform homa at night. The mantra is:
Oṃ cāmuṇḍe amuka-piśāca-kuru svāhā. For those who practice the *vaśīkaraṇa* rite.
If one wishes to cause all who see it to give rise to a heart of joy,
and to subjugate, hook, and summon— whether male or female, including devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, yakṣiṇīs,
as well as spirits and ghosts— [one should do so].
Should there be enemies who commit harmful acts,
may they all turn their minds toward joy;
may all Buddhas protect, mindfully attend to, and empower them.
This is called the rite for summoning and inspiring affection.
One who performs this rite shall wear red garments.
Facing west, with both knees raised and feet joined together, this is called the Samantabhadra posture (*samantabhadrāsana*).
One should contemplate the deity, as well as the offerings of incense, flowers, food, drink, fruit, lamps, candles, the ground, and so forth.
All [the implements] shall be red in color.
From the sixteenth day to the twenty-third,
one should recite the mantra three times each day and perform homa at night, using the summoning mantra as follows:
Oṃ jvale jvalani amukaṃ vaśīkuru svāhā. As for the *abhicāruka* rite:
it is for one who has committed the five *ānantarya* sins.
They slander the Vaipulya Mahāyāna,
destroy the Buddha-nature,
rebel against their sovereign, and bring confusion to the True Dharma.
One should arouse deep compassion for such a person and perform a rite of subjugation using donkey dung,
camel dung, or the ashes of cremated corpses.
Use it to smear the altar.
When performing this rite,
one should wear black or green clothing.
Facing south, squat with the left foot pressing upon the right.
Visualize the deity as black in color.
Offer flowers that are foul-smelling, lacking fragrance, and black or blue in hue.
The food, drink, incense, flowers, cakes, lamps, candles, ground,
and so forth that are offered should all be black or blue in color,
from the twenty-third day of the month until the end of the month.
Perform the recitation during the two periods of midday and midnight.
At night, perform the homa with the following mantra:
*HŪṂ JALEŚVARA JĀṄGULI AMUKASYA PĀRANAM KĀRAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ*. Next, the method for painting the image of the Buddha-mother Jāṅgulī is explained.
Take an uncut white cotton cloth that is free of hair and fur,
and hang it against a clean wall;
first, one should smear the altar.
One should offer arghya and food as an act of worship according to one's ability.
The painter should receive the eightfold precepts and, remaining pure, paint the image.
Among the pigments used, no glue derived from animal skins should be employed.
One should prepare the colors in a new vessel and paint an image of the Buddha-mother Cundī,
her body yellowish-white, seated in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Seated upon a lotus flower,
his body is adorned with a circular halo and draped in fine gauze,
like the robes of a bodhisattva of the ten pāramitās.
Both the upper and lower garments are white.
Furthermore, they wear celestial robes, shoulder-lets, necklaces, and crowns;
on their arms, they all wear bracelets and spiral arm-rings.
Dāna-hui wears jeweled bracelets;
the image has three eyes on its face and eighteen arms.
The two upper hands form the gesture of preaching the Dharma;
the second right hand bestows fearlessness,
and the third hand holds a sword.
The fourth hand holds a jeweled garland;
the fifth palm grasps a fruit;
and the sixth hand holds a battle-axe.
The seventh hand holds a hook;
the eighth hand holds a vajra;
the ninth hand holds a rosary.
The second left hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel banner;
the third hand holds a blossoming red lotus flower;
the fourth hand holds a water flask (*kamaṇḍalu*).
The fifth hand holds a noose;
the sixth hand holds a wheel;
the seventh hand holds a conch shell.
The eighth hand holds a precious vase;
the ninth hand holds a Prajñāpāramitā manuscript.
Below the lotus, a pool of water is depicted.
In the pond, Nanda the Nāga King and Upananda the Nāga King support a lotus seat;
on the left side, paint the practitioner performing recitation.
Holding an incense burner in his hand, he gazes up at the Noble One.
Out of compassion for the practitioner who recites the mantra,
the Buddha-Mother Cundī looks down upon him from beneath her eyes.
Above, two devaputras from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens are depicted:
one is named Kusumoda,
who holds a flower garland and leans downward.
Having descended from the void to make offerings to the Sage,
and having completed the painted image,
one should, according to one's means, invite seven monks in the order of their seniority.
Make offerings,
illuminate with light, recite incantations and prayers of aspiration, and offer praise.
Beneath the image, one should inscribe the verse on the origination of the Dharma-body (dharmakāya).
Place the image in a shrine room for secret worship,
covering it with silk;
when reciting the mantra, remove the silk covering.
Having completed the acts of prostration, offering, and recitation, cover [the image] with silk and take care not to let anyone see it. Why?
Because you have received from your master the ritual manual and the method for painting the image.
If one transmits this to others so that they may behold its form,
and it falls into the hands of Māra, one must maintain strict secrecy.
(From the *Dhāraṇī Sūtra Spoken by the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*)
